trade: boat captain who carries the plantation's crop to Lilmoth
spot: at the plantation's north-east edge by the goats, waiting for a load
backstory: Reads-The-Shallows runs a flat boat that carries Hereguard's crop to Lilmoth. She waits at the north-east edge of the plantation for the next load. She knows every channel between here and the walls and charges for each.
temperament: Brisk, practical and proud of her craft; impatient with landsmen.
manner: Clipped, nautical words; calls strangers 'passenger' and every place by how many turns of the channel it is.
wants: A full load and a fair wind before the plantation's steward changes his mind about the price.
grudge: The big ship's crew at the wreck to the south, who lost their vessel and still tell people she ran it aground.
notices: Weather, water depth and whether a stranger can sit in a boat without tipping it.
opinions: Thinks Lifts-The-Sacks is the only hand who loads properly; thinks the soldiers, Hard-Scale and Rakhee-Tul, guard the wrong side of the plantation; thinks Lilmoth Dock is a mess of small craft.
secret: She cannot read a chart and steers by memory and song.

trade: plantation hand who keeps the house's yard and stores
spot: in the yard by the plantation house on its west side, between the barrels and the benches
backstory: Hurz-Weel keeps the yard and the stores of the plantation house. He stands by the house because the steward wants a hand within call. He was born on the plantation and has never been further than Lilmoth.
temperament: Dutiful, anxious and a little self-important; worries about everything he is responsible for.
manner: Fussy, repeats instructions back, calls strangers 'visitor' and asks if they have business at the house.
wants: The stores counted and right before anyone checks them.
grudge: The manor servants Neeta-Lei and Mazei-Tul, who sit about while he does the heavy work.
notices: Who goes near the barrels and what they carry away.
opinions: Admires Looks-At-Books for her learning; resents Neeta-Lei and Mazei-Tul; thinks Reads-The-Shallows overcharges.
secret: Two of the food barrels are short, and he has been eating from them.

trade: plantation hand and loader
spot: in the middle of the plantation among the goats and chickens, between the house and the workbenches
backstory: Lifts-The-Sacks loads the plantation's crop and does whatever heavy work is left. He stands in the middle of the yard because every job passes him. He is working off an owing of months for a debt his uncle ran up.
lore: story/lore/topics/labour-and-bondage.md:68-77, :97-99 (an owing passes with a household); story/lore/extrapolation/gap-register.md:145 (QA7, Owing gangs hired to Hereguard)
temperament: Cheerful, strong and resigned; refuses to be pitied.
manner: Plain short sentences and a laugh at the end; counts in nushmeekos; calls strangers 'you' and the goats by name and talks to the goats more than to people.
wants: To finish his months by the next flood and go home to his tribe.
grudge: His uncle, dead now, whose debt he carries.
notices: Strength and posture; he can tell what a stranger has carried for years by their shoulders.
opinions: Likes Reads-The-Shallows, who thanks him; thinks Hurz-Weel fusses; is wary of the soldiers, Hard-Scale above all.
secret: He has counted his months himself and thinks the ledger has added three that he never owed.

trade: street seller of food and small goods to the plantation's hands
spot: on the plantation's east side near the cooking spit, where the hands eat
backstory: Salith sells food and small goods to the plantation's hands where they come to eat. She stands near the spit because hungry people buy. She came from Lilmoth to sell and stayed because the plantation has no other seller.
temperament: Motherly and blunt; scolds her customers and gives them credit.
manner: Warm, bossy, calls everyone 'hatchling' whatever their age, and ends with 'Eat something.'
wants: The hands to pay what they owe her before the next boat leaves.
grudge: The plantation's steward, who takes a cut of her sales for 'the use of the yard'.
notices: Who is thin, who is sick and who has not eaten today.
opinions: Mothers Okan-Wul; thinks Tumeesh is lazy and sweet; thinks Uleesh, who sells her fish, the most honest man outside the walls.
secret: She lets Lifts-The-Sacks eat free and writes his share on the steward's account.

trade: plantation hand who builds and mends the huts
spot: near Salith on the east side of the plantation, by the huts he keeps standing
backstory: Okan-Wul builds and mends the hands' huts on the plantation's east side. He stays near Salith's stall between jobs. He is young and wants to build something that will not rot in a season.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:42-45 (Imperial houses sank in the soft ground)
temperament: Earnest, restless and a dreamer; full of plans, short on patience.
manner: Talks with his hands, starts sentences with 'What if', calls strangers 'stranger' and asks what buildings look like where they come from.
wants: Good timber and someone to show him how stone is laid.
grudge: The house, which gets dry stone walls while the hands get reed huts.
notices: Joints, rot, roofs and how a stranger's boots are made.
opinions: Thinks Salith is the plantation's real headwoman; finds Hurz-Weel a fusspot; admires the stone wall on the east edge more than anyone else does.
secret: He has been taking boards from the carpenter's bench at night to build a hut of his own.

trade: fisher of the shallows below Lilmoth's walls
spot: in the open water south of the walls, among the lily pads where the fish feed
backstory: Uleesh fishes the shallows below Lilmoth's walls and sells his catch inside. He lives outside because the rent inside is more than fish pay. He has fished the same water for twenty years and talks to it.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:39 (shallow water); story/lore/regions/murkmire.md:29-31 (fish of Oliis Bay)
temperament: Content, superstitious and stubborn; nothing hurries him.
manner: Slow, plain sentences, often about the water as if it were a person; calls strangers 'dry-foot'.
wants: A good night's catch and nobody splashing about his lily pads.
grudge: The slaughterfish, which take his catch off the line, and the people who throw scraps that bring them.
notices: Ripples, splashes and anything that has been in the water; he can tell a swimmer from a wader.
opinions: Thinks the plantation at Hereguard pays its hands too little; buys his bait from Salith at Hereguard and likes her; thinks Lolmoth's walls keep out the wrong people.
secret: He feeds the old giant crab in the shallows to the south-west and believes it keeps the slaughterfish off.

trade: plantation hand who watches the flood water and the paddies' far edge
spot: at the north-east edge of the plantation, beyond the huts, where the water comes in
backstory: Tumeesh watches the water at the north-east edge of the plantation and warns when it rises. He stands out beyond the huts because the flood comes from there. He was sold on to Hereguard's labour from a broker in Lilmoth and does not know who holds his months now.
lore: story/lore/extrapolation/gap-register.md:145 (QA7: a Lilmoth broker hires an Owing gang to Hereguard); story/lore/topics/labour-and-bondage.md:90-96
temperament: Melancholy, gentle and absent; drifts off mid-sentence.
manner: Slow, fragmentary sentences with long gaps; calls strangers 'you' and asks what the sky looked like where they came from.
wants: To know who holds his months, so he knows who to pay.
grudge: The broker in Lilmoth who sold him on without telling him.
notices: Clouds, water level and birds; a stranger who comes from upriver.
opinions: Is grateful to Salith; thinks Lifts-The-Sacks too cheerful to be real; has never spoken to the soldiers and does not mean to.
secret: He keeps a knotted cord, one knot a day, and it no longer agrees with anyone's ledger.

trade: house servant at the plantation house
spot: by the plantation house, near the bed and benches on its south side
backstory: Neeta-Lei keeps the plantation house clean and its linen folded. He stays near the house in case he is called. He takes pride in the house as if it were his own.
temperament: Prim, proud and secretly kind; looks down on the field hands and feeds them scraps.
manner: Formal, careful sentences, calls strangers 'guest' and talks of the house as 'we'.
wants: Visitors to wipe their feet and the meat barrels kept away from the linen.
grudge: Hurz-Weel, who tramps mud through the house.
notices: Clothes: stains, tears, cut and cloth, and what they say about the wearer.
opinions: Thinks Mazei-Tul is idle; thinks Looks-At-Books is the only person here worth talking to; disapproves of Salith, who feeds the hands on credit.
secret: He has tried on the house's best clothes in the dresser more than once.

trade: house servant who keeps the plantation's horses
spot: on the north side of the plantation house, close to the horses
backstory: Mazei-Tul is a house servant who has made himself the keeper of the horses. He stands on the north side because the horses are there and the work in the house is not. He would rather be a rider than a servant.
temperament: Lazy in the house, devoted in the stable; sulky until you mention horses.
manner: Mumbles, then talks fast and bright about animals; calls strangers 'rider' whether they ride or not.
wants: To ride the saddled black horse to Lilmoth and back without being missed.
grudge: Neeta-Lei, who reports him every time he slips out.
notices: Mounts, saddles and boots with stirrup wear; how a stranger treats an animal.
opinions: Thinks Neeta-Lei is a tattletale; likes Lifts-The-Sacks, who helps with the feed; thinks Lilmoth too crowded for a horse.
secret: He has named every horse and cow on the plantation and talks to them at night.

trade: headman of the marsh village south-west of Lilmoth Dock
spot: beside the village cooking spit, the middle of his people
backstory: Flaa Heet leads a handful of families who live on the open marsh outside Lilmoth rather than pay its rents. He stands by the cooking spit because that is where every quarrel and every catch ends up. He wants no seat on the merchant council and says so before anyone offers.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:62-66 (merchant council; elders settle quarrels); :39 (shallow water)
temperament: Patient and weighty; he lets a silence run until the other person fills it, and he decides slowly and does not change his mind.
manner: Speaks in short, complete sentences and often in 'we' for the village; calls a stranger 'walker' and ends a ruling with 'So it is.'
wants: A dry season for the stores and one more boat, so the children stop wading to the fish barrels.
grudge: The merchants of Lilmoth, who send collectors for a tariff on fish that never passed their gate.
notices: Whether a stranger's boots are wet to the knee (they came over the marsh) or dry (they came by the dock), and whether they look at the food barrels.
opinions: Thinks Tseeta haggles too hard and is good for the village anyway; is fond of Peeks-Under-Boats and pretends not to be; considers the sellswords on the shore track (Haxal-Tei's band) a fire waiting for dry grass.
secret: He keeps a tally of every favour the village owes and is owed, scratched on the underside of his chair, and he has never let one go.

trade: a hatchling of Flaa Heet's village who runs errands and gets under feet
spot: the north edge of the village, where he can see the boats and the path to the fish barrels
backstory: A hatchling of Flaa Heet's village, small even for his age. He hangs about the north edge because that is where the boats come in and where nobody tells him to carry things. He wants to be a boat captain and practises by bossing frogs.
temperament: Bold, nosy and easily bored; he asks three questions for every one he answers.
manner: Talks fast in short bursts, repeats a word he likes ('huge', 'huge'), and calls any stranger 'big one'.
wants: To be taken out in the rowboat to the north-east, just once, without his mother knowing.
grudge: The fish barrels, because carrying to them is his chore and they smell.
notices: Weapons, boots and anything shiny; he will tell a stranger exactly what they are carrying.
opinions: Thinks Flaa Heet knows everything; thinks Hums-To-The-Rain sings too much; is scared of Deep-In-His-Cups and says he is not.
secret: He hid a pretty stone under the rowboat by the village and tells everyone he lost it.

trade: stall seller of food and small goods for the village
spot: at her stall on the north side of the village, the first stall anyone walking in from the dock meets
backstory: Tseeta sells the village's surplus to whoever walks in from the dock: fish, roots and small goods. She chose the north side so she meets buyers before Okeeh-Jas does. She is saving for a stall inside Lilmoth's walls and tells nobody how close she is.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:39-41 (a boat trade economy); census JobStreetVendorFaction
temperament: Sharp, quick and competitive; friendly exactly as long as you are buying.
manner: Brisk, counts on her claws as she talks, calls strangers 'buyer' whether they buy or not, and closes with 'Good trade.'
wants: To sell out before the light goes, and to beat Okeeh-Jas's takings for the day.
grudge: Okeeh-Jas, who undersells her on purpose and smiles while doing it.
notices: A buyer's purse before their face; who looks hungry; whether coin is new.
opinions: Respects Flaa Heet but thinks he is too soft on debts; thinks Okeeh-Jas is a thief with a stall; thinks Soulrest to the east are where real money is.
secret: She buys some of her stock from the thieves on the shore track and does not ask where it came from.

trade: net-mender and gatherer of the village
spot: on the west side of the village, between the spit and the second hearth, where the nets dry
backstory: Hums-To-The-Rain mends the village's nets and gathers what grows on the marsh. She works on the west side where the nets dry between the two hearths. She came from a tribe inland years ago and has never said which one.
lore: story/lore/topics/labour-and-bondage.md:108-116 (traits fade far from a tribe's Hist); story/lore/lilmoth.md:39
temperament: Gentle and dreamy, slow to anger and slow to answer; kind to everyone and close to no one.
manner: Soft, unhurried sentences, hums between them, calls strangers 'traveller' and says 'mm' when she agrees.
wants: Enough dry rope to finish the big net before the next rain.
grudge: Whoever cut a hole in her best net on purpose last season; she suspects Okeeh-Jas's hatchling cousin, and is probably wrong.
notices: Plants: what is ripe, what has been picked, and what a stranger has in their pack that grew somewhere else.
opinions: Thinks Flaa Heet carries too much alone; likes Peeks-Under-Boats and lets him tease her; thinks the marsh north of the village is kinder than Lilmoth's walls.
secret: Her colours have faded since she left her tribe, and she paints her frill with berry juice so no one asks why.

trade: stall seller of food and small goods, south side of the village
spot: at her stall on the south side of the village, near the boat landing
backstory: Okeeh-Jas sells food and small goods from the south stall, where the rowboat comes in. She trades with anyone who lands, and she likes the gossip as much as the coin. She married into the village and still talks like the city.
temperament: Cheerful, gossipy and shrewd under it; she laughs at most things, including her own prices.
manner: Chatty, long run-on sentences broken by 'you see?', calls strangers 'you' until she likes them and drops city slang.
wants: News: who came in, who left, who owes whom; she trades it as readily as fish.
grudge: Tseeta, who started the rumour that her fish is old.
notices: Gossip on a stranger's face: a fresh cut, a tired walk, a ring that does not fit.
opinions: Thinks Tseeta is too serious to be good at selling; finds Flaa Heet dull and wise; thinks Deep-In-His-Cups knows more than he lets on.
secret: She grew up in Pusbottom and left owing a moneylender there; she has never gone back through the walls.

trade: sellsword and brawler, the fists of a band of three
spot: at the band's camp on the shore track south-west of Lilmoth Dock, by the bedrolls
backstory: Haxal-Tei fights with his fists for whoever pays the band. He camps on the shore track with Heem-Tsal and Keeps-Both-Edges because the dock will not hire them and the city will not let them in armed. He is the one who talks terms.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:62-63 (council employs guards); :80-82 (foreigners kept to the docks once)
temperament: Loud, easy-going and quick to swing; holds no grudge longer than a bruise lasts, except one.
manner: Blunt and hearty; short sentences, cracks his knuckles mid-speech, calls strangers 'customer'.
wants: Paid work for the band this week, before Heem-Tsal walks off to find better company.
grudge: The council's guards, who turned the band away from the dock gate for being 'unlicensed blades'.
notices: How a stranger stands: weight, reach and which hand they favour.
opinions: Trusts Keeps-Both-Edges with his life and his purse; thinks Heem-Tsal is cleverer than all of them and too proud; thinks Deep-In-His-Cups is good company and a bad debt.
secret: He has never won a fight against Keeps-Both-Edges and lets the band believe it was a draw.

trade: battle-mage of fire, the band's spell and its scholar
spot: a few paces from the band's bedrolls on the shore track, on the side away from the others
backstory: Heem-Tsal casts fire for the band and reads whatever he can get. He stands a little apart from Haxal-Tei and Keeps-Both-Edges because he finds their talk tiresome. He joined them for passage south and has not yet found a reason to leave.
temperament: Proud, curious and a little contemptuous; warms up at once to anyone who asks a real question.
manner: Long precise sentences, corrects people's words, calls strangers 'ojel' (non-Jel speaker) without malice, and says 'Precisely.'
wants: A look inside the Dwemer ruin down the coast, and someone to carry the lamp.
grudge: The tree-minders of Lilmoth, who refused to let him sit by the city's Hist and take notes.
notices: Magic: a stranger's staff, the burn on their sleeve, whether they move like a caster.
opinions: Thinks Haxal-Tei is a good man with an empty head; respects Keeps-Both-Edges's discipline; has heard of Looks-At-Books at Hereguard and wants to see her shelf.
secret: He failed his trials at a mages' school and the robe he wears is borrowed from the one who passed.

trade: swordsman with two blades, the band's watch
spot: beside Haxal-Tei at the band's camp, facing the track so nothing comes up it unseen
backstory: Keeps-Both-Edges fights with a blade in each hand and keeps the band's watch. He stands facing the track so he sees anyone coming from the dock or the marsh. He was a guard once and will not say for whom.
temperament: Quiet, watchful and dry; slow to trust and loyal once he does.
manner: Few words, often just a fact and a nod; calls strangers 'you there' and answers questions with questions.
wants: To get the band off this shore track before the dead come down from the walls one night.
grudge: The man who hired the band last and paid in promises; he has not said a name.
notices: Exits, the ground between him and a stranger, and whether their hands stay still.
opinions: Thinks Haxal-Tei talks too much and fights well; thinks Heem-Tsal will get them all killed for a book; keeps an eye on Waits-For-Lanterns by the leeks.
secret: He still carries his old guard token and takes it out when he thinks no one is looking.

trade: drinker and talker, of no settled trade
spot: sitting out on the shore track south-west of Lilmoth Dock, where the guards do not bother him
backstory: Deep-In-His-Cups was a boatman once and is now mostly a drinker. He sits on the shore track because the dock guards move him on and nobody else does. He watches the dock all day and remembers more of it than he lets on.
temperament: Maudlin and friendly in turns; generous with stories, mean with his bottle.
manner: Rambles, loses the thread and finds it again, calls strangers 'fellow' and saves 'friend' for those who have stood him a drink, and is the one Argonian here who slurs his words together.
wants: Another drink, and someone to listen to the story of the boat he lost.
grudge: The boat-master who sacked him for a sinking that was not his fault, he says.
notices: Who comes and goes at the dock; boats and their loading; anyone carrying a bottle.
opinions: Loves Haxal-Tei, who buys; is wary of Keeps-Both-Edges, who watches; thinks Okeeh-Jas the kindest seller on the marsh.
secret: He did sink the boat, drunk, and has never said so sober.

trade: thief and scavenger of the dock's edges
spot: among the leeks on the shore north of the band's camp, close enough to the dock to watch it
backstory: Sheeh-Vos scavenges what the dock loses and steals what it does not. He crouches among the leeks so he looks like a gatherer to anyone passing. He works with Waits-For-Lanterns and does not like him.
temperament: Jumpy, greedy and sly; quick to smile, quicker to run.
manner: Whispers even when no one is near, talks out of the side of his mouth, calls strangers 'cousin' and says 'eh?' after a claim to see if it landed.
wants: To get to the bodies at the dock's east end before anyone official does.
grudge: Waits-For-Lanterns, who takes the larger share because he 'planned' it.
notices: Pockets, purses and locks; whether a stranger's pack is heavy.
opinions: Thinks Waits-For-Lanterns is a coward; thinks Tseeta pays fair for what she does not ask about; avoids Keeps-Both-Edges's eye.
secret: He has already taken a ring off one of the dead and is afraid it is cursed.

trade: thief who works the dark, a planner of small jobs
spot: a few paces east of Sheeh-Vos among the leeks, nearest the dock
backstory: Waits-For-Lanterns plans small thefts and waits for dark to do them. He stands nearest the dock, where he can count the lanterns and the guards between them. He thinks of himself as a professional fallen on a slow season.
temperament: Cool, patient and vain about it; despises haste in others.
manner: Measured, almost polite; long pauses; calls strangers 'honoured guest' with a little bow and never says yes or no outright.
wants: A partner with nerve; Sheeh-Vos has none.
grudge: The Pusbottom fence who cut him off after one bad night.
notices: Light: where the lanterns are, where the shadows fall, who carries a torch.
opinions: Thinks Sheeh-Vos is greedy and will hang them both; thinks Haxal-Tei's band would be useful if they could keep their mouths shut; wants nothing to do with Flaa Heet's village, which watches its barrels.
secret: He is afraid of the dark water and has never once swum, which no Argonian he knows would believe.

trade: soldier in the Lilmoth council's pay who guards the plantation's south side
spot: on the south side of the plantation by a bench, facing the water and the shore
backstory: Hard-Scale is a soldier in the pay of Lilmoth's merchant council, posted to guard Hereguard's south side, where the crop is grown that Lilmoth buys. He stands facing the water because whatever comes, comes from the shore. He takes the job more seriously than it deserves.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:62-64 (the merchant council employs guards); story/lore/regions/murkmire.md:71 and extrapolation/settlement-register.md:53,83 (Hereguard's crop, which Lilmoth buys)
temperament: Stern, rigid and humourless; believes in rules because they are rules.
manner: Clipped, formal orders rather than sentences, calls strangers 'citizen' and asks their business first.
wants: Nothing to happen on his watch, and to be seen to have stopped it.
grudge: Rakhee-Tul, who was given the easier post and sleeps on it.
notices: Weapons drawn or carried loose, and anyone walking where they should not.
opinions: Thinks Rakhee-Tul is slack; distrusts Tumeesh for staring; respects Looks-At-Books without knowing why.
secret: He is afraid of the giant crab in the shallows and keeps his post well back from the water.

trade: soldier in the Lilmoth council's pay who guards the plantation's south side with Hard-Scale
spot: a few paces north of Hard-Scale on the plantation's south side, nearer the yard
backstory: Rakhee-Tul is in the pay of Lilmoth's merchant council and guards the plantation's south side with Hard-Scale, where the crop is grown that Lilmoth buys. He stands a little nearer the yard where the shade and the gossip are. He took the post for the pay and has stopped pretending otherwise.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:62-64 (the merchant council employs guards); story/lore/regions/murkmire.md:71 and extrapolation/settlement-register.md:53,83 (Hereguard's crop, which Lilmoth buys)
temperament: Easy-going, cynical and talkative; does the least he can and does it well enough.
manner: Wry asides, shrugs, calls strangers 'boss' and gives advice nobody asked for.
wants: His pay on time and an evening off in Lilmoth.
grudge: Hard-Scale, who reports him for sitting down.
notices: Who is new, who is in a hurry and who might be worth a coin to let pass.
opinions: Thinks Hard-Scale will have a fit one day; likes Salith's cooking; thinks the wreck to the south is full of things nobody has bothered to take.
secret: He has been to the wreck and taken a silver piece from it, and left the rest for fear of being seen.

trade: bookseller and seller of paper and writing things
spot: by the tables on the west side of the plantation house, where she keeps her books out of the rain
backstory: Looks-At-Books sells books, paper and ink from a table by the plantation house. She keeps to the west side, under cover, because damp ruins stock faster than thieves. She came to Hereguard because the house buys paper for its ledgers, and she reads everything she sells before she sells it.
lore: story/lore/extrapolation/settlement-register.md:83; story/lore/topics/labour-and-bondage.md:84-89 (the ledgers kept by estates); census JobMerchantFaction
temperament: Reserved, wry and exacting; warm only to readers.
manner: Precise, slightly bookish, quotes titles, calls strangers 'reader' and says 'Mind the pages.'
wants: A buyer for the four volumes of The Argonian Account together, not one at a time.
grudge: The house's steward, who buys ledgers from her and pays a season late.
notices: Ink on fingers; whether a stranger reads or only looks at pictures.
opinions: Finds Neeta-Lei good company; thinks Heem-Tsal, the mage on the shore, will want her shelf and cannot afford it; thinks Hurz-Weel cannot read and pretends to.
secret: She has read The Lusty Argonian Maid more times than any other book she sells and blushes if asked about it.

trade: boat captain at Soulrest east of Lilmoth Dock
spot: at the head of Soulrest between the cooking spits and the north door, where boats tie up
backstory: Seeks-The-Channel runs a boat out of Soulrest east of Lilmoth Dock. She waits at the head of the landing between fares. She chose Soulrest over Lilmoth Dock because nobody here asks for a licence.
temperament: Easy, generous and a talker; a born host.
manner: Big friendly sentences, tells you three places when you asked for one, calls strangers 'traveller' and says 'Easy water.'
wants: A fare to Alten Merihall, where the money is.
grudge: The bears in the hills to the south-east, which took her goat last season.
notices: Where a stranger is going; whether they need a boat and can pay for one.
opinions: Thinks Xeeh-Nah is the best hand on Soulrest; feels for Feldril Nethri and will not say so loudly; thinks Lilmoth Dock is all guards and no business.
secret: She ferries goods for the thieves on the shore track on moonless nights.

trade: seller of food and small goods at Soulrest
spot: at the south-west side of Soulrest near the houses, where people come out to buy
backstory: Ushaa-Mei sells food and small goods to Soulrest's families and anyone who lands. She keeps to the south-west side, between the houses. She is Soulrest's memory for prices and holds everyone to last season's.
temperament: Dry, sceptical and fair; distrusts newcomers and trades fairly with them anyway.
manner: Short, flat statements and a sniff; calls strangers 'outsider' and prices by memory.
wants: The cows kept out of her stall.
grudge: Seeks-The-Channel, who brings in sellers from the coast to undercut her.
notices: Short weight, bad coin and anyone handling the goods without buying.
opinions: Thinks Seeks-The-Channel is too friendly to be honest; likes Plaits-The-Reed; keeps Little-Gecko out of the stock.
secret: She wants to leave Soulrest and has never been further than Lilmoth Dock.

trade: a hatchling of Soulrest
spot: in the middle of Soulrest between the chairs and the cooking fire, where the grown-ups talk
backstory: Little-Gecko is a hatchling of Soulrest who goes where the grown-ups talk. She sits in the middle by the fire so she hears everything. She wants to be a boat captain like Seeks-The-Channel.
temperament: Shy at first, then fearless; asks very serious questions.
manner: Whispery, careful sentences; calls strangers 'sir' or 'miss' because Ushaa-Mei told her to.
wants: To see the bears, from far away.
grudge: Cow-Chaser, who scares the cows on purpose and blames her.
notices: Animals and faces; whether a stranger smiles back.
opinions: Adores Seeks-The-Channel; thinks Cow-Chaser is a pest; is fond of Feldril Nethri, who carves her toys.
secret: She keeps a toy boat Feldril Nethri carved for her hidden from the grown-ups.

trade: reed-weaver of Soulrest, maker of mats and baskets
spot: on the south-west side of Soulrest near the houses, at her weaving
backstory: Plaits-The-Reed weaves mats and baskets for Soulrest's families and the boats. She sits on the south-west side near the houses, out of the wind. She is a widow and talks about her husband as if he had gone fishing.
lore: story/lore/lilmoth.md:42-45 (Argonian building of reed and wood)
temperament: Calm, sad and observant; kind in a quiet way.
manner: Low voice, sentences that trail off, calls strangers 'child' even when they are older.
wants: Good reeds from the south marsh, and company in the evening.
grudge: The sea, which took her husband.
notices: Hands, knots and craft; whether a stranger makes things or only buys them.
opinions: Likes Ushaa-Mei; thinks Xeeh-Nah should marry; worries about Feldril Nethri, who is far from any home.
secret: She still sets a place at the table for her husband.

trade: a hatchling of Soulrest
spot: at the north side of Soulrest near the cooking spits, where he can reach the cows
backstory: Cow-Chaser is a hatchling of Soulrest and the reason the cows run. He hangs about the north side near the spits, where food falls. He wants to be a warrior and practises on cattle.
temperament: Loud, cheeky and fearless; never still.
manner: Shouts, boasts, calls strangers 'warrior' hoping they will show him a sword.
wants: To see a real fight, or at least a real sword.
grudge: Ushaa-Mei, who chased him off her stall.
notices: Weapons and scars; he asks about both.
opinions: Thinks Little-Gecko is a baby; thinks Xeeh-Nah is the strongest person alive; is scared of Feldril Nethri for no reason he can give.
secret: He fell in the water last month and could not swim back, and Xeeh-Nah pulled him out.

trade: dock hand who hauls and ties up for the boats
spot: on the south-east side of Soulrest by the benches, where cargo is set down
backstory: Xeeh-Nah hauls cargo and ties up boats at Soulrest. He works the south-east side where loads are set down on the benches. He is strong, slow-spoken and owed money by half Soulrest.
temperament: Steady, shy and stubborn; gentle with children and short with bosses.
manner: One-line answers, long pauses, calls strangers 'ojel' if they are not Argonian and 'kin' if they are.
wants: To be paid by the ship crew who left their cargo at the big ship to the west.
grudge: Whoever hired Feldril Nethri's months; it takes the paid work off free hands.
notices: Loads, knots and whether a stranger's pack is too heavy for them.
opinions: Thinks Seeks-The-Channel talks too much and is honest; fond of Cow-Chaser; uneasy about Feldril Nethri and ashamed of being uneasy.
secret: He knows the chest by the big ship has never been claimed and has not opened it out of fear.

trade: Dunmer labourer at Soulrest working off an owing of months
spot: at the north end of Soulrest by the north door, kept apart from the families
backstory: Feldril Nethri is a Dunmer labourer working off an owing of months at Soulrest. He stands at the north end because he is put there and is not welcome by the fire. He came to Black Marsh to trade, lost a cargo, and was assessed months he cannot see the end of.
lore: story/lore/topics/labour-and-bondage.md:68-77, :94-96 (owings extended by food); :135 (dock crews); .claude/skills/dialogue-write/voices.md (Dunmer history in Black Marsh)
temperament: Bitter, proud and exhausted; courteous out of habit and scornful underneath.
manner: Long formal sentences in the Dunmer way, calls anyone not Dunmer 'outlander' and himself 'a guest of this marsh' with a dry edge.
wants: To learn who holds his months, and how many are left.
grudge: The Argonians who assessed his debt, and the food they charge back to it.
notices: Ledgers, tallies and who is lying about numbers; he was a trader once.
opinions: Is grateful to Seeks-The-Channel and Little-Gecko; thinks Xeeh-Nah an honest man who looks away; despises Soulrest and respects its people.
secret: He knows his family's house once traded in Argonian slaves, and he believes this owing is the debt coming due.

trade: village child who minds the rowing boat
spot: by the water at the village's middle, between the lily pads and the benches
backstory: Ree-Nakka is a hatchling of Low-Reed Village who has decided the rowing boat is hers to guard. She sits at the water's edge west of the benches and counts who comes and goes. The village is small enough that she knows every face in it.
lore: story/lore/extrapolation/gap-register.md:144 (QA6, Low-Reed Village); story/lore/regions/murkmire.md (small tribal villages with strong identity)
temperament: Bold, nosy and certain she is in charge of something.
manner: Quick questions in a row, never waits for an answer; calls a stranger 'you, tall one'.
wants: To be let out in the rowing boat alone.
grudge: Ixa-Mee, who told the grown-ups she pushed the boat out.
notices: Feet: who walked in through the water and who came dry.
opinions: Thinks Mends-The-Nets is the cleverest person in the village; thinks Ixa-Mee is a tattler; thinks Jaa-Kur is too small to play.
secret: She did push the boat out once, and lost the pole.

trade: village child who fetches for the net-mender
spot: beside the benches on the village's east side, close by Mends-The-Nets
backstory: Ixa-Mee runs errands for Mends-The-Nets and sleeps in the bamboo hut north of the benches. She is shy of strangers and tells the grown-ups everything. She was hatched in Low-Reed Village, as was everyone she knows.
temperament: Shy, careful and a stickler for rules.
manner: Whispers, answers in as few words as she can, says 'stranger' and looks away.
wants: A cord of her own to knot, like the net-mender's.
grudge: Ree-Nakka, who calls her a tattler.
notices: Whether a stranger's hands are empty.
opinions: Adores Mends-The-Nets; is afraid of Hulee-Tah's temper; thinks Ree-Nakka will drown one day.
secret: She is afraid of the water past the lily pads.

trade: net-mender
spot: between the two benches on the village's east side
backstory: Mends-The-Nets mends the village's nets on the benches by the workbench. She has done it since she was Ixa-Mee's size and taught half the village its knots. She has never wanted to live anywhere but Low-Reed Village.
temperament: Patient, dry and hard to impress.
manner: Slow, even sentences, often a saying about knots; names a stranger 'traveller' and keeps working while she talks.
wants: Cord: good cord, and more of it than the village can make.
grudge: Hulee-Tah, who borrowed her best net to roof his hut.
notices: Torn clothes, frayed straps, anything she could mend.
opinions: Fond of Ixa-Mee; thinks Ree-Nakka will lead the village or ruin it; thinks Xeech-Utsei talks to the trees more than to people.
secret: Her eyes are going, and she knots by touch now.

trade: pole-fisher of the north water
spot: among the lily pads on the village's north-west side, between the giant trees
backstory: Xeech-Utsei fishes the still water north-west of the huts with a pole and a long patience. He thinks the giant trees above him know more than the village gives them credit for. He brings disputes to the tree-minder sooner than anyone.
temperament: Calm, pious and a little solemn.
manner: Pauses before he answers; speaks of the trees as if they listen; calls a stranger 'walker'.
wants: A quiet morning with no one splashing.
grudge: Hulee-Tah, who cut reeds by his water and scared the fish.
notices: Whether a stranger moves quietly.
opinions: Trusts Pays-Late above everyone; thinks Mends-The-Nets is wise; thinks Hulee-Tah is loud.
secret: He has caught nothing for days and has been eating the net-mender's bait fish.

trade: hut-builder
spot: outside his bamboo hut on the village's west side
backstory: Hulee-Tah builds and patches the village's bamboo huts, his own first. He stands outside it on the west side, where he can see the water and the rowing boat. He went once to trade at the road-houses and came back sure the village does things better.
lore: story/lore/extrapolation/gap-register.md:144 (QA6, Low-Reed Village); story/lore/extrapolation/settlement-register.md (interior trade: food, tools, passage over coin)
temperament: Loud, proud and quick to take offence; quicker to forgive.
manner: Big statements, laughs at his own jokes; calls a stranger 'outsider' to their face.
wants: Bamboo enough to raise a second hut before the rains.
grudge: Mends-The-Nets, who still wants her net back.
notices: How a stranger's gear is made and whether he could make it better.
opinions: Likes Jaa-Kur, who helps him; thinks Xeech-Utsei is idle; thinks the root-herald gives too much away in trade.
secret: The net is still in his roof, and he has no wish to give it back.

trade: village child who carries bamboo for the hut-builder
spot: in the shallows among the lily pads on the village's south-west side
backstory: Jaa-Kur is the youngest hatchling who still follows the hut-builder about, carrying what he is given. He plays in the shallows south of Hulee-Tah's hut when there is nothing to carry. He has never been past the giant trees.
temperament: Eager, trusting and easily delighted.
manner: Tumbling sentences joined with 'and'; calls a stranger 'big one' and asks what they brought.
wants: To be let carry the long poles, not just the short ones.
grudge: Ree-Nakka, who will not let him near the rowing boat.
notices: Anything shiny on a stranger.
opinions: Worships Hulee-Tah; thinks Ree-Nakka is bossy; thinks Mends-The-Nets is very old.
secret: He has hidden a carved bead under a lily pad and checks it every day.

trade: dock worker who hauls the lines
spot: at the north end of the street, past the Dwemer ruin, by a bench
backstory: Hauls-Wet-Rope hauls lines and loads for whoever pays at the north end of Helstrom. She took the name the dock bosses gave her and kept it. She grew up on the Panther River and came to Helstrom for the work.
temperament: Tired, blunt and fair.
manner: Plain words, grumbles as she talks; calls a stranger 'you there'.
wants: A day off her feet.
grudge: Namorine, who takes the easy loads.
notices: Hands: who has done hard work and who has not.
opinions: Thinks Namorine is lazy but honest; thinks Gih-Xaleel is the only one keeping order; thinks the north end is forgotten.
secret: She is saving to buy a boat of her own and has told no one.

trade: boatman who waits for a fare by the ruins
spot: on the street just north of the Dwemer ruins
backstory: Namorine is a boatman who waits by the ruins for anyone who wants carrying along the water. He keeps the name his mother gave him, which no one in Helstrom can place. He has carried fares as far as the Stormhold side and does not care for it.
temperament: Easygoing, gossipy and vain.
manner: Long, chatty answers that wander off; calls a stranger 'passenger', hopefully.
wants: A fare that pays well and goes somewhere he likes.
grudge: Stormhold folk, who haggle him down every time.
notices: Whether a stranger has coin and somewhere to be.
opinions: Thinks Hauls-Wet-Rope works too hard; likes Bejeen-Ul's company; thinks Helstrom is the finest city there is.
secret: He cannot swim.

trade: labourer who patches the old stonework
spot: in the street right beside a Dwemer ruin, west of the houses
backstory: Bejeen-Ul patches the old stonework of Helstrom's streets for the assembly's levy. He stands by the ruin he is meant to be mending. He says the city is older than anyone's story of it, and the lore agrees.
lore: story/lore/helstrom.md:6-8, 26-30 (active since the late First Era)
temperament: Gentle, slow and stubborn.
manner: Few words, long pauses, a habit of patting the stone; calls a stranger 'visitor'.
wants: Stone that does not crumble when he touches it.
grudge: The levy, which pays him late.
notices: Cracks: in walls, in boots, in stories.
opinions: Likes Namorine's talk; thinks Gih-Xaleel is fair; thinks the ruins should be left as they are.
secret: He has not mended anything in a month; he just stands by the ruin.

trade: levy warden who keeps the gate
spot: at the gate, between the Dwemer ruins
backstory: Gih-Xaleel is a warden of Helstrom's levy, the guard that receives and redistributes for the assembly. He keeps the gate between the ruins and decides who goes in. Helstrom has never been taken, and he means to see it stays so.
temperament: Hard, watchful and dutiful.
manner: Short orders and flat statements; calls a stranger 'outlander' and expects them to state their business.
wants: A quiet gate and a levy that does as it is told.
grudge: The Imperial histories that call Helstrom's guard brutes.
notices: Every weapon, every face, and which way a stranger came from.
opinions: Trusts Azum-Kai; thinks Teeka-Xul is useless; thinks Sells-Dear is sharp but honest.
secret: He keeps a list of everyone who passes the gate, and has lost the first half of it.

trade: porter at the dock who tallies what comes off the boats
spot: between the dock and the old stone columns, by an iron door
backstory: Counts-Every-Crate carries and tallies what is landed at the dock below Helstrom. He took a city name for city work and keeps every count in his head. He was born in the interior and still trusts a sack of food over a purse.
temperament: Exact, wary and fond of order.
manner: Numbers in every answer; short, counted sentences; calls a stranger 'newcomer' and asks what they carry.
wants: A season where the counts come out even.
grudge: The boat captain, Sells-Dear, who he says lands more than she declares.
notices: What a stranger carries and how heavy it is.
opinions: Respects Gih-Xaleel's discipline; thinks Teeka-Xul is slow; thinks Okan-Zish and Wuleen-Taza are idle rafters.
secret: He cannot count past a hundred without his fingers and hides it.

trade: soldier who watches the bridges
spot: on the bench by the bridges, between the houses and the water
backstory: Teeka-Xul is a soldier of Helstrom's levy posted to the bridges on the landing's side. He sits more than he stands. He came out of the marsh to serve and means to go back to it.
temperament: Unhurried, sly and hard to rattle.
manner: Drawls, answers a question with a question; calls a stranger 'walker' and watches their hands.
wants: A posting with shade.
grudge: Azum-Kai, who reported him for sitting.
notices: Who crosses the bridges, and how often.
opinions: Thinks Azum-Kai is too keen; thinks Counts-Every-Crate is a fusser; thinks the landing is the quietest post in Helstrom.
secret: He sleeps on watch at midday and has never been caught.

trade: soldier of the levy at the stone tower
spot: at the foot of the stone tower by the bridge
backstory: Azum-Kai keeps the levy's watch at the stone tower over the landing. He took the post young and takes it seriously. He knows Helstrom's name for a dangerous guard and means to keep it.
temperament: Stiff, earnest and proud of the uniform.
manner: Formal, full sentences; calls a stranger 'traveller' and asks their business first.
wants: To be noticed by the levy warden and moved to the gate.
grudge: Teeka-Xul, who sits on watch.
notices: Weapons, and how they are worn.
opinions: Admires Gih-Xaleel; distrusts the rafters Okan-Zish and Wuleen-Taza; thinks Teeka-Xul shames the levy.
secret: He has never drawn his blade on anyone.

trade: Agaceph rafter of the landing crew
spot: by the stone tower at the landing, beside Wuleen-Taza
backstory: Okan-Zish is an Agaceph rafter who poles goods across the landing's water with Wuleen-Taza. Agaceph travel by thin rafts made for one, and he has never trusted anything bigger. The two of them work the landing's crew together.
temperament: Restless, boastful and quick to change the subject.
manner: Talks fast and big, then goes vague; calls a stranger 'dry-foot'.
wants: More work than the boat captain gets.
grudge: Sells-Dear the boat captain, who takes the trade his raft should have.
notices: Whether a stranger looks like they would pay to cross.
opinions: Sticks by Wuleen-Taza; thinks Sells-Dear is greedy; thinks Azum-Kai watches them too closely.
secret: Trade has been so thin he has thought of leaving the landing.

trade: Agaceph rafter of the landing crew
spot: by the bridge near the stone tower at the landing
backstory: Wuleen-Taza poles a raft on the landing's water with Okan-Zish. She is Agaceph, from the deep interior, where food and tools count for more than coin. She does the crew's bargaining, because Okan-Zish cannot keep a straight face.
temperament: Shrewd, cool and guarded.
manner: Short, level answers, gives nothing free; calls a stranger 'customer' whether they are or not.
wants: Enough trade to keep the crew together.
grudge: Sells-Dear, who undercuts every price she names.
notices: What a stranger could pay, in coin or in kind.
opinions: Protects Okan-Zish and calls him a fool; thinks Sells-Dear is a cheat; thinks Teeka-Xul is harmless.
secret: She keeps a store of dried food under the bench in case the crew breaks up.

trade: householder who keeps a house by the tower
spot: outside her own door, west of the street
backstory: Weesa-Nur keeps a house a little west of the street, with a stone tower behind it. She sells what she can spare to the boats at the dock. She has lived in Helstrom all her life and has opinions about all of it.
temperament: Sharp-tongued, house-proud and nosy.
manner: Asks as much as she answers; calls a stranger 'you' and looks them up and down.
wants: Her doorstep left clean.
grudge: Sells-Dear, who ties up too close to her house.
notices: Dirt on a stranger's boots and where they put their feet.
opinions: Distrusts Sells-Dear; thinks Gih-Xaleel is too stern; thinks the dock folk are all thieves.
secret: She talks to the house when no one is about.

trade: boat captain who trades by boat from Helstrom
spot: by a house door on the west side of the street
backstory: Sells-Dear runs a boat and trades by it out of Helstrom. She took a city name to deal with city buyers, and lives up to it. The landing's rafters hate her for taking their trade; she thinks they should get a boat.
temperament: Confident, mercenary and amused by everyone.
manner: Prices in everything she says, a laugh at the end; calls a stranger 'buyer'.
wants: The landing's trade, all of it.
grudge: Okan-Zish and Wuleen-Taza, who badmouth her to every customer.
notices: What a stranger would pay, and whether they would notice being overcharged.
opinions: Thinks Weesa-Nur is a busybody; respects Gih-Xaleel; thinks Counts-Every-Crate miscounts on purpose.
secret: She sells below cost on the landing side just to starve the rafters out.

trade: soldier of the levy who guards the hall
spot: indoors in the hall behind the iron door near the gate
backstory: Tuxeel-Zan is a soldier of Helstrom's levy posted inside the hall behind the gate's iron door. He prefers a roof to the street. He has heard every story told about Helstrom's guard and repeats the worst ones.
temperament: Gruff, bored and secretly kind.
manner: Grunts, one-line answers; calls a stranger 'you' and nods at the door.
wants: A change of post that is not the street.
grudge: Gih-Xaleel, who keeps him indoors.
notices: Wet feet on the hall's floor.
opinions: Resents Gih-Xaleel but obeys him; thinks Azum-Kai will go far; thinks Stormhold folk are soft.
secret: He feeds a marsh rat that lives under the hall.
